items.text: REFERRED TO CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PROTECTION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to clear and conspicuous
pricing practices regarding mandatory junk fees
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7783

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to clear and
conspicuous pricing practices regarding mandatory junk fees

 
PURPOSE:

To eliminate hidden junk fees by requiring sellers to display the total
price of a good or service, inclusive of all mandatory fees.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one refers to the title of the act, the "New York Junk Fee
Prevention Act."

Section two amends the general business law by adding a new section
396-yy, which includes three subsections. Subsection 1 defines "mandato-
ry fee" while making exceptions for taxes and certain delivery fees. It
also defines "total price" as the full price that a consumer must pay,
inclusive of all mandatory fees associated with the transaction.
Subsection 2 requires any person or entity doing business in the state
to clearly and conspicuously display the total price of a good or
service, inclusive of all mandatory fees, in every offer or advertise-
ment, not just toward the end of the payment process. Subsection 3
relates to the enforcement of this section, authorizing the attorney
general to bring actions and seek injunctions. It also allows private
individuals adversely affected by violations of this section to sue for
damages.

Section three amends the general business law by adding a new section
349-g, which lists new deceptive pricing methods related to junk fees.
Such methods shall be deemed deceptive practices within the meaning of
section 349 and be enforced as such.

Section four relates to the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Consumers have become all too familiar with the hidden costs of junk
fees. Rarely can someone complete a transaction without getting hit with
a service fee, fulfillment fee, convenience fee, or some other hidden
charge. These junk fees raise the prices of everything from concert
tickets and hotel bookings to car rentals and internet services.

Junk fees are particularly frustrating not just because they make things
more expensive but also because they are imposed on consumers in unfair
and deceptive ways. Rather than disclose all mandatory fees up front -
thus making it clear what the total price will be at the outset - compa-
nies lure customers in with a seemingly low price tag, then surprise
them with added fees at the end of the payment process.  By keeping
these charges hidden, companies have made it more difficult to compare
prices and search for the best deals, leading many consumers to surren-
der to an artificially inflated price.

In addition to harming consumers, junk fees place honest businesses at a
competitive disadvantage. Companies that immediately disclose the total
price of their products inclusive of all mandatory fees - will often
lose customers to bad faith actors who advertise a lower charge but
actually charge more. By allowing junk fees to proliferate, the market
ends up rewarding companies that engage in predatory bait-and-switch
tactics while punishing those that are transparent with consumers.

The actual, total price of a good or service should never come as a
surprise; it should be clearly and conspicuously displayed from the
outset, accounting for all mandatory fees from the very beginning of the
transaction. This would empower shoppers to assess their options more
efficiently and make better-informed decisions. It would also bring some
much-needed fairness into our free-market system. By cracking down on
deceptive advertising practices and requiring transparent pricing, this
bill will finally do away with junk fees and provide both consumers and
businesses much-needed relief.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become law.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7783B

SPONSOR: GIANARIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to clear and
conspicuous pricing practices regarding mandatory junk fees

 
PURPOSE:

To eliminate hidden junk fees by requiring sellers to display the total
price of a good or service, inclusive of all mandatory fees.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one refers to the title of the act, the "New York Junk Fee
Prevention Act."

Section two amends the general business law by adding a new section
396-yy, which includes three subsections.

Subsection 1 defines "mandatory fee" while making certain exceptions.
It also defines "total price" as the full price that a consumer must
pay, inclusive of all mandatory fees associated with the transaction.

Subsection 2 requires any person or entity who solicits or facilitates a
purchase directly from a consumer to clearly and conspicuously display
the total price of a good or service, inclusive of all mandatory fees,
in every offer or advertisement in most circumstances, and disclosure of
mandatory fee exceptions prior to accepting payment.

Subsection 3 relates to the enforcement of this section, authorizing the
attorney general to bring actions and seek injunctions. It also allows
private individuals adversely affected by violations of this section to
sue for damages.

Subsection 4 sets forth compliance for those: providing broadband in
complying with the relevant federal regulations; financial institutions
which comply with listed federal standards; those imposing surcharges on
sales transactions where a consumer elects to use a credit card instead
of other payment means; and food service establishments which display
the percentage of automatic and mandatory gratuity to be charged.

Subsection 5 provides that those subject to subdivision four of section
25.07 of the arts and cultural affairs law, and air carriers, shall not
be subject to the provisions of this section.

Section three relates to the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Consumers have become all too familiar with the hidden costs of junk
fees. Rarely can someone complete a transaction without getting hit with
a service fee, fulfillment fee, convenience fee, or some other hidden
charge. These junk fees raise the prices of everything from concert
tickets and hotel bookings to car rentals and internet services.

In addition to harming consumers, junk fees place honest businesses at a
competitive disadvantage. Companies that immediately disclose the total
price of their products inclusive of all mandatory fees - will often
lose customers to bad faith actors who advertise a lower charge but
actually charge more. By allowing junk fees to proliferate, the market
ends up rewarding companies that engage in predatory bait-and- switch
tactics while punishing those that are transparent with consumers.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

summary: Establishes the "New York junk fee prevention act"; requires clear and conspicuous pricing practices regarding trash junk fees.
